When creating an MKLocalSearch.Request object yourself, set the [`naturalLanguageQuery`](mklocalsearch/request/naturallanguagequery.md) property to an appropriate search string, as in the following example:

segments.normalizedSource: ```swift let searchRequest = MKLocalSearch.Request() searchRequest.naturalLanguageQuery = "coffee" // Set the region to an associated map view's region. searchRequest.region = myMapView.region let search = MKLocalSearch(request: searchRequest) search.start { (response, error) in guard let response = response else { // Handle the error. } for item in response.mapItems { if let name = item.name, let location = item.placemark.location { print("\(name): \(location.coordinate.latitude),\(location.coordinate.longitude)") } } } ```

```objc MKLocalSearchRequest *searchRequest = [[MKLocalSearchRequest alloc] init]; searchRequest.naturalLanguageQuery = @"coffee"; // Set the region to an associated map view's region. searchRequest.region = self.myMapView.region; MKLocalSearch *search = [[MKLocalSearch alloc] initWithRequest:searchRequest]; [search startWithCompletionHandler:^(MKLocalSearchResponse *response, NSError *error) { if (response) { for (MKMapItem *item in response.mapItems) { CLLocationCoordinate2D coordinate = item.placemark.coordinate; NSLog(@"%@: %f,%f", item.name, coordinate.latitude, coordinate.longitude); } } else if (error) { // Handle the error. } }]; ```
